nodes.text: You grow up in a family that already decided everything for you.

options.label: Obey and meet expectations
Argue and stand your ground
Grow up ordinary, never standing out

nodes.text: Rules give a sense of safety. But where do they lead?

options.label: Study as hard as you can, join the system
Find a quiet rebellion within the rules
Discover an early pull toward art

nodes.text: Every disagreement pulls you further from home.

options.label: Leave the family too soon
Chase thrills at the edge of the law
Seek comfort in faith as everything falls apart

nodes.text: School days are full of choices no one warns you about.

options.label: Cheat
Study hard
Get into fights
Silently endure the mockery

nodes.text: Something is being born inside you that has no use yet.

options.label: Games you invent yourself
Melodies that won't let go
Frames that assemble themselves in your head
Stories begging to be written down

nodes.text: The edge of the law tempts those who have nothing to lose.

options.label: Commit a real crime
Volunteer for the front, far too young for it
End up behind bars over one reckless night

nodes.text: Silence becomes your most frequent word.

options.label: Find a secret outlet no one will know about
Slowly stop feeling anything at all

nodes.text: The secret life becomes the only real one.

options.label: Keep it to yourself until the end
Let someone finally see the real you

nodes.text: Feeling became too painful, so you stopped.

options.label: Live out your days apart from everyone
Channel the emptiness into a hunger for power
Seek relief in faith

nodes.text: Home is behind you now. The road is ahead.

options.label: Look for odd jobs
Trust the road completely

nodes.text: Odd jobs give you neither money nor roots.

options.label: Keep barely staying afloat
Start writing down the stories of people you meet
Start composing melodies out of boredom in the underpass
Use street smarts for a career in power

nodes.text: Cities change, faces change. Home never appears.

options.label: Freeze one day under the open sky
Invent whole worlds to keep from losing your mind
Film what's happening on a found camera, finding meaning in it
Use a drifter's charisma to eventually seize power

nodes.text: Crime becomes a way of life.

options.label: Work alone, small-time
Join an organized group

nodes.text: Small jobs bring no big score — only big risk.

options.label: Trust your luck one more time
Legalize your earnings through a business of your own

nodes.text: The group offers protection, but demands total loyalty.

options.label: Climb all the way to the top
Launder the money through a real business
Use the underworld's connections for legitimate power

nodes.text: The walls decide who you'll become next.

options.label: Cooperate with the administration
Endure it in silence
Find accomplices for an escape
Go to war to shorten your sentence

nodes.text: Cooperation opens the door a little earlier.

options.label: Get out early and try to live differently
Become an informer for good

nodes.text: Every day here wears something away in you.

options.label: Get out broken, but alive
Not survive another day

nodes.text: The escape plan is ready. The forest waits on the other side of the fence.

options.label: Run and hide in the forest
Back out at the last moment

nodes.text: Food runs out faster than hope.

options.label: Act together, share the last of it equally
Do the unthinkable to survive
Seek redemption in faith after what happened

nodes.text: War changes the rules of the game for everyone.

options.label: Serve in the rear
Ask to be sent straight to the front
Emigrate instead of serving
Use the chaos of war to seize power

nodes.text: The rear is safer, but your conscience won't rest.

options.label: Stay here until the war ends
Ask to be sent to the front after all

nodes.text: The front line leaves no time to think.

options.label: Save a wounded comrade under fire
Disobey an order
Fight bravely and without mercy

nodes.text: You're dragging your comrade through gunfire. Every step could be your last.

options.label: Carry him out alive
Die before you can get him out

nodes.text: The order contradicts everything you believe.

options.label: Disobey and save the innocent
Face a court-martial

nodes.text: You fight in a way that silences questions of morality.

options.label: Win at any cost, losing part of yourself
Hold on to your humanity at the last moment

nodes.text: You'll come back a different person, if you come back at all.

options.label: Live to make it home
Not survive what you became

nodes.text: Home is the same. You are not.

options.label: Seek help, talk about what happened
Stay silent and carry it alone
Seek refuge in faith
Express what happened through art

nodes.text: Money decides faster than principles.

options.label: Build an empire, whatever the cost
Run the business honestly, slowly
Use capital to buy power

nodes.text: Success grows, and loneliness grows with it.

options.label: Trade everything personal for success
Stop before you lose yourself

nodes.text: The business grows slowly, but it's built on trust.

options.label: Hand it to your children, having grown old at the helm
Lose everything in one bad year
Turn to illegal schemes to win it back

nodes.text: Betraying your own principles opens doors that open no other way.

options.label: Go all the way, whatever it costs
Keep up the appearance of principles

nodes.text: Every decision now shapes other people's fates.

options.label: Strike a deal with your conscience for the sake of greatness
Someday lose everything you built on lies

nodes.text: The mask of principle holds — until it's truly tested.

options.label: Pass the test, giving up something small
Be exposed publicly

nodes.text: Science promises no recognition, only truth.

options.label: Devote your life to fundamental work that will be understood later
Chase quick, practical success
Sell your discovery to whoever offers power

nodes.text: The lab becomes more of a home than home itself.

options.label: Finish the work, even if it takes your whole life
Burn out halfway, never finishing

nodes.text: Practical gain arrives faster than truth.

options.label: Grow rich from your discovery
Discover your discovery was used for something you never wanted
Seek redemption in faith

nodes.text: The body becomes a tool, and records become the goal.

options.label: Push for success at the limit of your strength
Suffer an injury that changes everything

nodes.text: Victories bring fame, but it doesn't last.

options.label: Leave at your peak, become a coach
Cling to fame longer than you should

nodes.text: Your body no longer obeys the way it used to.

options.label: Find a new meaning outside sport
Fail to cope with the loss of who you were

nodes.text: Now you pass on what you know to others.

options.label: Raise students who will go further than you
Drink yourself away from irrelevance
Use your old fame to go into politics
Find comfort in faith instead of the bottle

nodes.text: An ordinary life demands choices too, just quieter ones.

options.label: Build a home and raise children
Search for more, unsatisfied with little

nodes.text: The years pass evenly, marked not by events but by habits.

options.label: Grow old surrounded by those you love
Realize one day you lost yourself along the way

nodes.text: Ordinary life starts to feel too small.

options.label: Run from the routine too late to start over
Find meaning in your children instead of yourself
Seek recognition beyond the family, in power
Seek meaning in faith rather than in the world

nodes.text: Faith promises meaning where none is visible anymore.

options.label: Give yourself to faith completely
Use faith only as comfort, nothing more

nodes.text: Service consumes everything that used to be yours.

options.label: Devote your life to serving others
Discover faith doesn't save you from doubt
Turn faith into a tool of influence over people

nodes.text: Faith stays close, but doesn't define you entirely.

options.label: Find peace in simple rituals
Lose your faith completely just when you needed it most

nodes.text: The new country is in no hurry to accept you.

options.label: Stay penniless, surviving day to day
Find humiliating but stable work without papers
Turn to illegal earnings, since there's no legal path

nodes.text: Hunger doesn't ask about pride.

options.label: Accept help, start over from nothing
Fail to hold on and break
Turn to crime, having lost hope of a legal path

nodes.text: Work without status grants no rights, only obligations.

options.label: Endure it for years, until you finally get papers
Break under the weight of exploitation

nodes.text: Without papers, legal paths are closed — only illegal ones remain.

options.label: Build an illegal but profitable trade
Grow rich enough to buy yourself legality and influence

nodes.text: The game you're designing means more to you than the paycheck for it.

options.label: Make an indie game alone, against all odds
Go work at a major studio for stability

nodes.text: There are no resources, but the vision feels more important than resources.

options.label: Work yourself to the bone to finish it alone
Gather a team of people just as obsessed
Give up, unable to bear the uncertainty
Release a game with a message the authorities call illegal

nodes.text: The project is almost done. You are not.

options.label: Release the game at any cost
Stop before it's too late
Seek refuge in faith, unable to bear the pressure
Get caught holding something illegal during the crunch

nodes.text: Stability exists, but the vision dissolves into other people's decisions.

options.label: Give in and do as you're told
Fight for your vision from inside the system
Climb the career ladder, forgetting about games

nodes.text: The melody in your head demands to be heard.

options.label: Play in underpasses and small clubs, honing your sound
Try to break into the big industry right away

nodes.text: The audience is small, but real.

options.label: Stay true to your sound, even without recognition
Break down one day from poverty and exhaustion
Write a song the authorities call a call to riot

nodes.text: The industry is ready to make you a star — on its own terms.

options.label: Agree to an image someone else invented
Refuse and stay yourself at the cost of your career
Use popularity as a springboard into power

nodes.text: Fame has arrived, but it doesn't quite belong to you.

options.label: Play the part for as long as it works
Fail to cope with the pressure and collapse
Seek refuge in faith, trying to fight the addiction
Get caught red-handed

nodes.text: The shots assemble themselves in your head faster than the money for a camera appears.

options.label: Shoot low-budget auteur films
Push into the big industry

nodes.text: Festivals value boldness more than budget.

options.label: Stay true to your authorial vision to the end
Spend years unable to find funding for the next film
Make a film the authorities call incitement

nodes.text: The studio is ready to make your film — if it becomes their film.

options.label: Compromise for the sake of distribution
Walk off the set, defending your vision
Use industry connections to enter power

nodes.text: The film hits theaters. It's no longer quite yours.

options.label: Accept it, keep making films on these terms
Leave the profession, unable to bear the compromises
Seek relief in addiction, and later — in faith
Get caught red-handed on set

nodes.text: The story inside you demands to be written down.

options.label: Write what matters to you, without thinking about sales
Write what sells

nodes.text: Publishers politely reject you, one after another.

options.label: Keep writing for the drawer, no matter what
Give up one day and burn the manuscripts
Publish a work the authorities declare illegal

nodes.text: The books sell, but they're not the ones you wanted to write.

options.label: Keep writing under someone else's name for the money
Someday write the real book under your own name
Use your pen's fame to write speeches for those in power
Seek refuge in faith, unable to bear the pressure of fame

nodes.text: What can't be said out loud can sometimes be told another way.

options.label: Write a book about the war
Make a film about what you went through

endings.text: You fade away slowly, alone, having never said what you needed to say.
You die knowing that at least one person saw the real you.
You're not found right away — the neighbors didn't notice the silence at first.
You collapse at some random construction site. No one even knows your name.
You freeze under the open sky, in a city whose streets you never learned the names of.
A bullet finds you on the doorstep of one last job — the siren sounds too late to matter.
Your own people are standing nearby at the exact moment it's more convenient for you to be gone.
Years later you die at home, quietly, in your sleep — the freedom you once earned had simply become ordinary.
Former cellmates find you first — before you manage to start a new life.
Your body walks free. Your heart stops a year later, quietly, in your sleep — part of you never really left the cell.
You don't survive another night — the body can't withstand what was done to it for too long.
Years later you die at home, in your own bed — a rare luxury for someone who once shared the last scrap of food in a forest.
You survive the forest. Years later your heart stops in your sleep — but your eyes never learned to close peacefully.
The war ends without a single shot fired your way — but the question of what you would have done at the front never lets go, even decades later.
Years later you're buried with honors — that day at the front became the defining moment of the life you lived afterward.
A bullet finds you before you can take the last step.
You die an old man, knowing for certain: that day, you did the right thing.
The court-martial leaves you no future, only a sentence carried out at dawn.
You don't survive what you became — the body can't carry the weight it held inside.
Years later you die at home, finally at peace with what you once saw.
Years later, the war still hasn't let go. Your heart stops quietly, in your sleep.
You choke on a bone from an exquisite fish at dinner on your own yacht — there's no one nearby who'd know what to do.
You die at home, surrounded by those you passed on not just the business, but the name.
The scandal takes everything down to the last item. Your heart can't survive the first truly cold winter with no heating.
A bullet finds you exactly where you least expected it — among the people you considered your own.
The scandal ends your career in a single night. Your heart can't survive the first day without a guard at the door.
You die in office, at a respectable age — only you ever knew the price of the compromises.
A crowd outside the courthouse — the last thing you see before your heart stops from shame and strain.
Your heart stops at work, in the middle of an unfinished project — one that others will finish, citing your name.
Years of work break off mid-sentence in a lab notebook.
You die in the comfort you built for yourself — quietly, in your sleep, in your own home.
You die never having forgiven yourself for what your discovery became.
You die at home, surrounded by students who long surpassed you — and that's the only thing that matters.
The body can't withstand what you used to try to drown out the emptiness.
You fall asleep and don't wake up — in a house full of people who will miss you.
You die never having found out who you might have become outside that house.
You die on the road, never having decided what exactly you were running from all those years.
You die among those you served your whole life — they will remember your name longer than you remembered it yourself.
You die with a question you never got an answer to.
You die quietly, in a familiar ritual, without fear and without an answer — just with peace.
You die feeling an emptiness where there used to be at least something.
After years of quiet life, your heart stops in your sleep, in a home that finally became yours.
You're found too late — frozen in an apartment with no heating, because there was no one left to pay for it.
Years later, now legal, your body gives in to the strain that had been building the whole time.
You collapse at the machine. The work won't stop for even a day.
You grew rich on something that can't survive daylight — and you die the same way, far from it.
The game ships and finds its small, devoted following — you die an old man, still answering letters from fans.
The project stays a folder on an old drive. You die without ever opening it again.
The game launches the same day your heart stops at your desk — you never get to read the reviews.
You die comfortably retired, looking at a game whose credits list your name as one of fifty.
You die never having broken the system completely — but something of what you envisioned survived in the final game.
You perform into deep old age for a small but devoted crowd — and slip away quietly, soon after your last show.
An overdose finds you before the next song does.
You die at the peak of fame, surrounded by people who know the image, not you.
You keep filming until the very end — the camera by your bed, even when you have strength for only one shot a day.
You die with a folder of unrealized scripts on your desk — not one of them ever became a film.
You die wealthy and forgotten — no one remembers the last film with your name on it.
Your main book is found and published only after your death — the one that made all the writing worthwhile.
The ashes of the manuscripts are all that's left of what you wanted to tell the world.
You die the author of dozens of names on other people's covers, and not one of your own.
Your heart stops in the middle of the street. No one even gets the chance to ask what happened.
